# Ridu 0.21.0

Image uploads take photos from current phones: Ridu reserves the memory image processing actually
uses, so 24- and 40-megapixel photos are no longer refused. `MaxImageDimension` stores a smaller
original, and remote image imports refuse IPv4-compatible IPv6 addresses.

## Security

- Importing an image with `uploadFromURL` refused private and special-use addresses, but accepted
  IPv4-compatible IPv6 addresses such as `::127.0.0.1` and `::169.254.169.254`, which reach the
  same hosts. Remote fetches now accept IPv6 only inside the global unicast block, `2000::/3`,
  without its special-purpose ranges.

## Changes

- `UploadConfig.MaxImageDimension` scales a JPEG or PNG original wider or taller than that many
  pixels down to fit before Ridu stores it, keeping its shape and never enlarging it. The scaled
  image replaces the stored file with its `width`, `height`, and `filesize`, the private source
  that crops start from, and the image sizes made from it. It is stored upright, without the
  camera's EXIF metadata. GIFs and smaller images keep their uploaded bytes. The value must be at
  least the width and height of every image size. See
  [Limit large images](https://riducms.com/docs/uploads/#large-images).

## Fixes

- Ridu reserved about twice the memory resizing an image used, so a photo over about 21
  megapixels needed more than the whole 512 MiB budget and was refused. The reservation now
  follows the work: for a JPEG, its chroma sampling, progressive coding and EXIF orientation. Image
  sizes are resampled through an intermediate of four bytes a pixel instead of 32. With sizes of
  800 and 1,600 pixels, a 24.5-megapixel photo reserves about 205 MiB instead of about 600 MB, and
  photos up to the 40-megapixel limit are accepted.
- The image budget is half of `GOMEMLIMIT` when you set it, and 512 MiB otherwise.
- An image over the budget fails with a message that tells the person uploading the most the
  server takes, ending, for example, `upload an image of at most about 18.3 megapixels`. An image
  over the 20,000-pixel or 40-megapixel limit says which.

## Upgrade

Update the Go module and all Ridu npm packages to 0.21.0 together, and rebuild the admin and
application binary. No contract changes.

Generated image sizes are resampled by a different library, so their pixels can differ slightly
from earlier versions'; their dimensions and crops are unchanged. Set `GOMEMLIMIT` a little below
your service's memory, for example `GOMEMLIMIT=900MiB` for 1 GB.

Ridu requires Go 1.26.9 or newer. Go 1.27.0 and 1.27.1 meet that minimum but still have the
standard-library vulnerabilities described in the 0.20.0 notes, so build and deploy with Go 1.26.9
or a later 1.26 release, or with Go 1.27.2 or later.
